gaps.note: A visible edit and stumble during the initial statement of the ask.

stage_a.note: Smiles and energetic vocal delivery convey strong enthusiasm and positive engagement throughout.
High energy, prominent hand gestures, and a bright vocal tone show strong engagement.
A friendly and inviting demeanor when engaging the sharks to try the products.

venture.description: An online gifting platform offering curated designer gift boxes containing flowers, chocolates, and other items.
venture.note: Founders mention both individual consumers and corporate gifting channels.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Introduces himself and the other two founders to the panel.

turns.speaker: F3
turns.summary: States the company name and the investment ask.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Notes that buying a gift is not always an easy process.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Asks the panel to recall the last time they had to order a gift for someone.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Highlights the common frustration of buying generic gift cards when nothing better is found.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Introduces Bouquet Bar as an elegant online gifting platform.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains the first steps of choosing a designer box and adding gifts.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Lists the various options available, such as chocolates, tea blends, and flowers.

turns.speaker: F3
turns.summary: Describes adding a custom note and sending the finished box.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Invites the sharks to help them bring the art of gifting to everyone.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Suggests moving past the pitch to try some amazing treats.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Jokes with Kevin about liking treats.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Jokes back at Lori about a moment on the lips.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Remarks that Kevin always says that phrase, but only to girls.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Hands out sample gift boxes to the panel while they admire the presentation.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks how a customer mixes and matches items for the boxes.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Explains the website process of selecting a box size and then picking specific items.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks how many different choices are currently available.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States that they have only been out for four months.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks to confirm they have only been in business for four months.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms four months and lists the twenty-two SKUs plus two bouquets they currently offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks about shipping, noting that the box is very heavy.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Compliments the beauty of the product before the sharks attack the numbers.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Repeats the question about how much it costs to ship the heavy box.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States that shipping currently costs around twelve to fifteen dollars.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks for the average cost to make the small box with product inside.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Provides the detailed costs to make and the retail prices for all three sizes of boxes.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks the founders how they got into this business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Shares his immigrant background, dropping pre-med to sell flowers, and starting a floral design company.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Explains his background in digital media and technology, and his marketing role in the new venture.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks how much revenue the floral design business does.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States that the other business does about three million dollars annually.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks if the investors are getting a piece of that other business in the deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Clarifies that they are not offering equity in the other business.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Teases the founder by saying that is just what he says.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks how customer acquisition cost is going to work for the new business.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: States their acquisition cost is about sixty dollars utilizing Google AdWords.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks to confirm that they are not making any money at all.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Begins to concede that as of right now they are not making money before being interrupted.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks what their revenues have been in the last four months.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States that revenues have been close to one hundred thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks how much of their own money is invested in the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States that they have invested six hundred thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks if there is any external money or just their own.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms it is just their own money.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks what the money was spent on.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Lists expenses including product development, a large facility, and three hundred thousand dollars in inventory.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Presses them on needing to lower the customer acquisition cost to ten or fifteen dollars.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Agrees that lowering the cost is their goal but says it will take time.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks who their target customer is.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Details their demographic breakdown of males and females aged thirty-five to fifty-five.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Adds that they want to teach people how to gift because people are scared to do it.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Calls out the similarity of their product to an established competitor, Sugarfina.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Argues that they are not a candy company like the competitor.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Points out that customers will find the competitor first and it is cheaper.

turns.speaker: F3
turns.summary: Emphasizes that they are flower experts, differentiating them from the candy company.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Insists they need to be more unique to beat the competition.

turns.speaker: F3
turns.summary: Acknowledges the issue and states he is currently designing new items for the next line.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Says she would invest if they had come in with more unique floral designs at a good price.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Praises their drive but exits because they haven't figured out the differentiation yet.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Agrees with Lori that the differentiation from competitors is not big enough and exits.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Explains that educating people on gifting is too hard and expensive, and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tries to pivot the conversation to other markets like corporate and wedding gifting.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Praises the quality but exits because he wants to invest in a business with a solved acquisition cost.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks if their corporate gift selling relies on salespeople or walk-ins.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms that it is all driven by salespeople.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks if those salespeople can go out and sell on commission.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees that they can have salespeople sell on commission.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks how flexible they are to come up with different designs.

turns.speaker: F3
turns.summary: States they are innovative and he would love to design more items.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Challenges their valuation, asking why they thought ten percent was enough equity to offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains they felt the valuation was fair given the work done, acknowledging they will need more money.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks what they are going to need more money for and when.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States they will need money for sales, operations, and staffing.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Challenges the need for a big staff in an e-commerce business, asking why they need to spend more.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Starts to explain that they don't think they need a lot more money before being interrupted.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks if the need for money is because it is all tied up in inventory.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Briefly denies that it is just inventory before being cut off.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Tells the founders they need to give up more equity or they won't get a deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Emphasizes their commitment, noting they have inventory ready to sell and can fulfill orders immediately.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Makes a non-negotiable offer to the founders.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Accepts Mark's offer without further negotiation.

exchanges.label: product mechanics and time in business

decisions.note: Hasn't figured out how to differentiate from competitors like Sugarfina.
Differentiation is not big enough to invest.
Educating people on gifting is too hard and costs a lot of money.
Wants to invest in scaling an already solved customer acquisition cost problem.

record.notes: The pitch includes a brief edit during the initial ask where the founder stumbles.
